newsitem.title: DUBAI: Rafsanjani says Iran's missiles for defensive aims.
newsitem.headline: Rafsanjani says Iran's missiles for defensive aims.

text.p: Iran is developing its missile capability but only for defensive purposes and has no intention of attacking any other country, President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani was on Monday quoted as saying.

"I agree with you on what is being said about our progress in the missile industry, but that is taking place within a pure defensive framework and we have no aggressive intentions against anybody," he said.
Rafsanjani was speaking in an interview with the Saudi-owned, London-based Asharq al-Awsat newspaper.

Recalling the 1980-88 war between Iran and Iraq when Iraq hit Iranian cities with long-range missiles, Rafsanjani said: "From this basis we cannot but use this (missiles) to protect ourselves, but we will not use missiles to attack any country."
Rafsanjani reiterated Iranian denials of U.S. allegations that Tehran was seeking to develop nuclear weapons.
"We have announced repeatedly that Iran's doors are open to whoever wishes to inspect (installations) and we assert that Iran is not trying to obtain nuclear weapons."
A German newspaper said on Friday Iran was developing missiles based on the Russian Scud and North Korean Nadong systems with a range of 5,500 km (3,500 miles).

Quoting unidentified western intelligence services, the Bild daily said the missiles were capable of hitting targets in Europe from bases in Iran and could carry a 770 kg (1,700 lb) payload of poison gas or bacteria.

The Iranian navy in November tested Chinese-built C-802 anti-ship missiles from one of its 10 Houdong patrol boats. U.S. officials had said Iran's acquisition of the radar-guided C-802 missiles, which they expect to be eventually operational on about 20 Iranian vessels, was a new dimension in the naval threat in the oil-rich region.

The United States has expressed growing concern since the 1991 Gulf War about what it describes as Iran's growing military capability and its aims in the region. The same concerns have been voiced by Iran's Gulf Arab neighbours.
